notes: Compressed proxy for a long hermes session: 4 plain prompts in ONE `hermes chat` REPL. Asserts the per-turn ready→working→ready arcs, no waiting anywhere, and a final settle to ready. BIRTH IS TWO PHASES because hermes creates its sessions row LAZILY at turn setup (run_agent.py _ensure_db_session, called from turn_context), not at REPL launch: before turn 1 the only observable row is the daemon's own proc-<PID> pre-session, which never goes working. Every post-birth phase is pinned to the store-backed session via new_session + session_id_prefix (hermes ids are YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) and same_session_as, so the pre-session cannot steal the birth and cascade failures. The working span is observable at all because hermes commits the inbound user row BEFORE the first LLM call (turn_context.py: 'Crash-resilience: persist the inbound user turn before the first LLM call'), so a watcher scan between that commit and the assistant finish_reason='stop' row sees LastEventType=user_message → working. model is left UNPINNED (the recording home's config.yaml decides it) and cost is NOT asserted (hermes reports 0.0 under billing_mode=subscription_included and irrlicht's capacity table has no pricing for gpt-5.6-luna, so 0 is correct); tokens are asserted non-zero because sessions.input_tokens/output_tokens are maintained per API call. No tool calls: the recipe is plain prompts, matching the scenario description and the claudecode sibling, so the scenario's 'includes at least one tool call' bullet is not covered by this cell.

text: `hermes chat` launches; the daemon's process matcher mints a proc-<PID> pre-session in ready. No store row exists yet — hermes writes its sessions row only at the first prompt.

Turn 1's prompt creates the store-backed session (id YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) and its inbound user row, driving that session to working. Across the rest of the run it never enters waiting — the recipe has no tool calls, so nothing reaches an approval gate.
Turn 1 ends: the assistant row lands with finish_reason='stop' and the SAME session settles working → ready.
Turn 2 prompt drives the same session ready → working.
Turn 3 prompt drives the same session ready → working.
Turn 4 prompt drives the same session ready → working.
Final turn ends; working → ready. The session reaches ready and is not stuck in any state.
